title: Pager-to-Postmortem Lifecycle and Incident Ecosystem Guide
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary:
This guide documents the end-to-end lifecycle from the initial pager alert through containment, customer communication, and formal postmortem. It defines handoffs, roles, runbook snippets, escalation ladders, status page and customer messaging templates, a lightweight postmortem rubric, and a game-day facilitation checklist. Use this as the canonical operational playbook for incidents that affect Redwood Inference production services.

Goals and scope:
- Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) to < 1 minute for P0 alerts.
- Reduce mean time to restore (MTTR) by enforcing clear handoffs and automated evidence collection.
- Ensure consistent customer communication and a fast path to post-incident learning.
- Scope: applies to all user-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated clusters, Private control plane).

Incident severity classification (quick reference):
1) P0 — Service down / major data loss / broad customer-impacting SLO breach
   - Symptom examples: 100% error rate for requests to /v1/generate; region-wide unavailability.
   - Target: Pager immediately; all-hands bridge within 15 minutes.
2) P1 — Severe degradation / partial outage impacting many customers
   - Symptom examples: tail latency > 5x baseline for > 5 minutes; degraded quantization path failing for a model group.
   - Target: Pager; bridge within 30 minutes; mitigation window 2 hours.
3) P2 — Single-customer degradation, non-critical regressions, or intermittent errors
   - Symptom examples: single tenant experiencing timeouts; latency SLO flapping.
   - Target: Notify on-call, cadence-driven engagement.
4) P3 — Low-impact issues, enhancements, and observations for future work

Roles and responsibilities (examples):
- Initial Responder (pager recipient): ack, gather first signals, execute immediate mitigations from runbook (owner: oncall SRE).
- Incident Lead (IL): coordinates bridge, decisions, and comms (owner: senior SRE/ops).
- Service Owner: deep diagnostic and code-level remediation.
- Customer Success Liaison: crafts and sends customer-facing updates.
- Postmortem Author: writes the blameless analysis and action items.

Pager -> Bridge -> Triage: a 6-step flow
1) Alert receives pager (0m): oncall ack within MTTA target. Collect alert ID, affected service, and key metrics.
2) Initial assessment (0–5m): responder runs the quick triage checklist (see runbook snippets). If service-down indicators present, escalate to IL.
3) Bridge creation (5–15m for P0, 5–30m for P1): start video/voice bridge, invite IL, service owner, platform, and CS.
4) Containment (15–45m): apply safe fallbacks (route to model variant, scale burst pools, enable degraded-mode caches). Document every change in the bridge notes.
5) Customer comms (15–60m): publish status page entry and send initial customer notice per template.
6) Resolution and verification (after containment): confirm metrics, remove mitigations in controlled fashion, schedule RCA/postmortem.

Quick triage checklist (copyable to pager message):
- Acknowledge pager with alert ID and ETA for first update.
- Verify service health: /health endpoints, metrics for request rate, error rate, queue depth.
- Check recent deploys (last 60 minutes) and config rollouts.
- Determine if fallbacks/route-to-variant exist and are safe to enact.
- If error rates > 30% or latency > 5x baseline, escalate to IL.

Runbook snippet: KV cache saturation (typical pattern)
- Symptom: sudden spike in tail latency with cache hit rate drop below 70%.
- Immediate safe actions:
  1) Disable aggressive prefetch/backfill tasks: `kubectl scale deployment cache-prefetcher --replicas=0 -n platform`
  2) Enable read-through cache fallback to CPU-backed L2: `config set service.cache.l2_enabled true`
  3) Apply rate limit to incoming model-requests: `redwoodctl throttle --service inference --limit 50rps`
- Evidence to collect (automated if possible): cache hit/miss histogram, pod CPU/GPU utilization, redis client connections, KV cache queue depth.
- Escalation: if latency not improving in 10 minutes, escalate to Service Owner and IL.

Escalation ladder (contact order):
1) Oncall SRE (pager)
2) Senior SRE (escalation)
3) Service Owner (engineering lead for the microservice)
4) Platform / GPU-fleet lead
5) Eng Manager / Incident Exec (for customer-impacting decisions)

Status page and customer communications
- Status page template (short):
  Title: [ONGOING] High error rate impacting inference API in us-west-2
  Impact: Partial or degraded request handling for hosted API customers using us-west-2.
  Update cadence: every 30 minutes until mitigation is verified.

- Customer email (initial) template:
  Subject: Service disruption affecting Redwood inference in us-west-2

  Body:
  Hello <CustomerName>,

  We are investigating increased error rates and elevated latency for inference requests in the us-west-2 region. Our on-call team has opened an incident (INC-<id>) and is actively working on containment.

  What we know now:
  - Affected scope: hosted API for models served in us-west-2 (approx X% of requests).
  - Customer impact: increased timeouts and failed requests for some models.
  - Next update: in 30 minutes or when materially changed.

  Actions we are taking: scaling dedicated pools, routing to variant models, and enabling degraded cache layer.

  We will follow up with a full post-incident summary.

  — Redwood Inference Support

- Customer follow-up template (post-incident brief): include root cause summary, timeline, impact assessment, actions taken, and action items with ETA.

Postmortem template (required fields):
- Title (short)
- Incident ID and severity
- Authors and reviewers
- Impact summary (customers, metrics, duration)
- Timeline of key events (minute resolution for first 2 hours)
- Root cause analysis (technical & systemic causes)
- Immediate mitigations and why they worked/didn't
- Action items (owner + ETA)
- Communication record and status page links
- Learning and acceptance criteria for closing the actions

Postmortem rubric (fast pass / needs deep dive):
- Fast pass (postmortem within 7 days, 1 owners meeting): incidents where root cause is clear and action items limited to 1–3 operational fixes.
- Deep dive (postmortem within 14 days, cross-team review): incidents causing data loss, P0 with ambiguous RCA, or any incident with > 10% revenue impact.

On-call rotations and shift best practices
- Standard rotation: 1-week primary oncall for SREs, 2-week secondary coverage for senior SRE.
- Handover checklist for shift start/end:
  - Confirm runbooks and recent deploys.
  - Check outstanding incident action items; escalate if overdue.
  - Sanity-check alerting thresholds and mute noisy alerts.
- Shadowing policy: new oncall members shadow primary for 2 rotations before full ownership.

Game day facilitation blueprint
- Purpose: validate runbooks, handoffs, and cross-team coordination for common failure modes (e.g., failover, KV-throttle, region egress failure).
- Frequency: quarterly per platform area (serving runtime, platform, private).
- Key roles: facilitator (ops lead), scorer (IL), observers (product/CS/security).
- Scenario structure:
  1) Inject: describe the simulated failure and initial signals.
  2) Observe: measure MTTA/MTTR and adherence to runbook steps.
  3) Score: use a 0–5 rubric for communication, technical mitigation, and documentation.
  4) Debrief: capture action items and update runbooks immediately.

Game day scoring rubric (example):
- Communication (0–5): clarity of status updates, cadence, and customer messaging.
- Technical mitigation (0–5): correctness and safety of actions taken.
- Evidence and logs (0–5): quality and completeness of data captured for RCA.
- Runbook fidelity (0–5): adherence to documented procedure.

Automation and evidence collection checklist
- Ensure alerts include trace IDs, request IDs, and relevant metric snapshots.
- Automate evidence capture: `metrics-snapshot --alert $ALERT_ID --time-window 10m`
- Store bridge notes in a canonical incident folder and link to postmortem.

Retention and post-incident follow-up cadence
- Postmortem draft: within 7 days (fast pass) or 14 days (deep dive).
- Action item reviews: within 14 days for minor items, 30 days for cross-team work.
- Runbook updates: enforce PR for any runbook exercised during an incident; change must include test or verification step.

Appendix: useful snippets and links
- Command to create a bridge and capture a screenshot of CPU/GPU heatmap:
```
bridgectl create --title "INC-<id> Redwood inference us-west-2" --participants @oncall @service-owner
metrics-snapshot --metric gpu_utilization --window 5m --out /tmp/INC-<id>-gpu.png
```

- Evidence collection checklist (copy into bridge notes):
  - Snapshot of error-rate, 50/95/99 latency, request rate
  - Recent deploy IDs and config revision numbers
  - List of active mitigations and rollback timestamps
  - Owner assignments for each action item

- Related internal pages:
  - SLO and error budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
  - Postmortem framework: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026

Contact and ownership
- Playbook owner: Priya Nair (ops/resilience lead)
- Review cycle: annual or after any P0 incident; reviewers: Ethan Brooks, Sofia Patel.

Change log:
- 2025-03-10: Created (initial lifecycle and templates).
- 2026-02-14: Added KV cache runbook snippet, updated MTTA/MTTR targets and game-day rubric.

End of guide.
